de11_life.topic: Elon Musk: birth, family, emigration, education, work status, citizenship, emerald mine

claims.text: Born 28 June 1971 in Pretoria to Errol Musk, an electromechanical engineer, and Maye Musk nee Haldeman, a model and dietitian born in Saskatchewan; siblings Kimbal and Tosca

Parents divorced 1979; at about nine he chose to live with his father, later regretted it and became estranged; his account of being beaten and hospitalised after a school fight, and of his father berating him; Errol denied this

Obtained a Canadian passport through his mother to avoid South Africa's compulsory military service; arrived in Canada June 1989; Queen's University 1990; transferred to Penn; Penn awarded BA physics and BS economics in 1997 though Musk said 1995; accepted to Stanford graduate program 1995, did not enroll; US citizen 2002
Musk in 2013 interview: left at 17 'in part, in order to avoid conscription in the army'; 'spending two years suppressing Black people doesn't seem to be a great use of time'

WaPo: arrived 1995 for Stanford program, never enrolled, began working at Zip2 Aug/Sept 1995 (his 2009 deposition); Mohr Davidow invested $3M in 1996 with 45 days to obtain legal work status; 2005 email to Eberhard and Straubel: 'no legal right to stay in the country'; work authorization around 1997, reportedly NAFTA category; Musk said 'gray area' (2013) and 'legally there' on a 'student-work visa' (2020); Musk did not respond
Musk on X after the report: 'I was in fact allowed to work in the US' and 'The Biden puppet is lying'

2020: 'American, but born in South Africa. Left by myself when I was 17.'; July 2023 post to Ramaphosa: 'They are openly pushing for genocide of white people in South Africa'; May 2025 called BEE 'Apartheid version 2'; Starlink licence dispute
Home Affairs minister Schreiber declined (March 2025) to disclose whether Musk, Thiel, Sacks are South African citizens, citing PAIA

Emerald mine: Musk 2014 father 'had a share in an emerald mine in Zambia'; 2019 'He didn't own an emerald mine & I worked my way through college'; 2023 'the fake emerald mine thing'; Errol to Isaacson: traded a plane for emeralds from an unregistered Zambian mine, 'none of it was legal'; Isaacson concluded Errol never owned a mine

de11_paypal.topic: Zip2, X.com, Confinity merger, ouster, PayPal sale

claims.text: Zip2 founded 1995 (as Global Link Information Network) by Elon and Kimbal Musk and Greg Kouri; city-guide software licensed to newspapers; Mohr Davidow invested $3M in 1996; Rich Sorkin became CEO and Musk CTO; failed CitySearch merger 1998; Compaq bought Zip2 in February 1999 for about $305M (other accounts $307M); Musk netted about $22M

Musk founded X.com in 1999; merged with Thiel and Levchin's Confinity in March 2000, keeping the X.com name; in September 2000, as Musk left on a fundraising trip and delayed honeymoon, executives delivered no-confidence letters and the board replaced him with Thiel; renamed PayPal 2001
Musk (Inc. 2007): 'I buried their hatchet'; 'Life is too short for long-term grudges'; on the ouster: 'It's not a good idea to leave the office when there are a lot of major things underway'
eBay completed its merger with PayPal on 3 October 2002 at 0.39 eBay share per PayPal share (about $1.5bn in stock; Musk 11.72%, about $175.8M per Wikipedia)
Musk bought back the x.com domain (not the company) from PayPal in July 2017

de11_state.topic: Tesla founding and co-founder settlement; SpaceX; public money; Starshield; NSSL; Golden Dome; Starlink in Ukraine

claims.text: Eberhard's suit over the founder title settled out of court Sept 2009; Eberhard, Musk, Straubel, Tarpenning and Wright agreed to be called co-founders; Musk: 'Without Martin's indispensable efforts, Tesla Motors would not be here today'

WaPo: at least $38bn in government contracts, loans, subsidies and tax credits over 20+ years; $6.3bn committed in 2024; 52 ongoing contracts could pay $11.8bn more; NASA says it has invested >$15bn in SpaceX; early NASA awards $278M (2006) and $1.6bn (2008); Tesla $11.4bn from regulatory credits since 2014, about a third of profits; $465M DOE loan in 2010, repaid within a few years; Nevada $1.3bn; New York $750M to SolarCity; Musk 2015 'If I cared about subsidies, I would have entered the oil and gas industry'; Shotwell 'We earned that'; excludes classified work
Reuters: SpaceX's Starshield unit building a network of hundreds of spy satellites for the NRO under a $1.8bn contract signed in 2021; separate from Starlink; NRO declined to comment on SpaceX's role
NSSL Phase 3 Lane 2 (4 April 2025): SpaceX $5.92bn for 28 missions, ULA $5.37bn for 19, Blue Origin $2.39bn for 7; firm fixed-price requirements contracts
Space Force 24 April 2026: 20 agreements to 12 companies including SpaceX and Anduril for Golden Dome space-based interceptor prototypes, combined potential $3.2bn, per-firm values not disclosed
EO of 13 Aug 2025 eased FAA launch-licence environmental reviews; Reuters: SpaceX 'potentially stands to be the single biggest immediate beneficiary'; signed months after the Musk-Trump falling-out

CNN excerpt of Isaacson (7 Sept 2023) said Musk ordered Starlink turned off near Crimea in 2022; Isaacson clarified: 'the Ukrainians THOUGHT coverage was enabled all the way to Crimea, but it was not'; Musk: 'emergency request from government authorities to activate Starlink all the way to Sevastopol', agreeing would have made SpaceX complicit in a 'major act of war and conflict escalation'
Oct 2022 Musk said SpaceX could no longer fund Ukraine's use (cost $80M), then walked it back; Pentagon confirmed 1 June 2023 it contracts with Starlink for Ukraine services, value withheld

9 March 2025 Musk: Starlink 'the backbone of the Ukrainian army', 'Their entire front line would collapse if I turned it off', 'Starlink will never turn off its terminals'; to Sikorski 'Be quiet, small man'; Poland pays about $50M a year, about half of ~42,000 terminals; Rubio: 'No one has made any threats'
Reuters (22 Feb 2025), three sources: US negotiators raised cutting Ukraine's Starlink access in minerals talks; Musk: 'This is false. Reuters is lying.'

1 Feb 2026: Ukraine's Fedorov announced only authorised Starlink terminals would work, unverified terminals disconnected, thanking SpaceX; Russians had reportedly used Starlink on Shahed drones; Musk said SpaceX's steps had likely stopped Russia's unauthorised use

Founders Fund invested $20M in SpaceX, announced 4 Aug 2008 after the third Falcon 1 failure (2 Aug 2008); managing partner Luke Nosek joined the SpaceX board; Musk accepted it 'as a precautionary measure'

de11_x.topic: Twitter purchase, co-investors, changes, government pressure both ways, xAI/Grok, 2025 and 2026 mergers

claims.text: Equity commitments for Twitter bid (filing, 5 May 2022): Ellison $1bn, Sequoia $800M, Binance $500M, Qatar Holding $375M, Fidelity $316M, Alwaleed pledged 34,948,975 shares; $7.14bn total; $54.20 a share, $44bn
Kingdom Holding and Alwaleed's office rolled over 34.9M shares worth $1.89bn and called themselves jointly the second-largest investor; QIA $375M; Dorsey rolled over ~$1bn

4 April 2022 9.2% stake disclosed; 14 April offer $54.20; 8 July tried to terminate; Twitter sued in Delaware 12 July; closed 27 October 2022; executives fired; ~half the workforce laid off 4 Nov 2022 (7,500 to about 1,500 eventually); journalists suspended Dec 2022 over ElonJet; rebranded X July 2023; $13bn bank debt
Trump account restored 19 Nov 2022 after a poll (51.8% yes); Musk 'Vox Populi, Vox Dei'; Trump had been suspended after 6 January 2021

Twitter Files from 2 Dec 2022 (Taibbi, Weiss, Shellenberger); Taibbi: 'no evidence - that I've seen - of any government involvement in the laptop story'; both Trump White House and Biden campaign made takedown requests; FBI reimbursements $3.4M for legal requests
Murthy v. Missouri, 26 June 2024, 6-3 (Barrett): plaintiffs lacked standing to enjoin federal officials accused of pressuring platforms; Alito, Thomas, Gorsuch dissented

May 2023 Twitter restricted access to some content in Turkey on the eve of the election at the government's demand; Musk: 'The choice is have Twitter throttled in its entirety or limit access to some tweets'; he 'repeatedly paints himself a free speech absolutist'
Brazil's Justice de Moraes ordered X blocked on 30 August 2024 for failing to obey orders (block profiles, name a legal representative, pay fines); lifted October 2024 after X paid the fines
28 March 2025: 'xAI has acquired X in an all-stock transaction'; xAI $80bn, X $33bn ($45bn less $12bn debt)
Reuters, 3 Feb 2026: SpaceX acquired xAI, SpaceX valued $1tn and xAI $250bn, largest M&A deal on record; IPO planned
xAI Series E $20bn (8 Jan 2026) with QIA and Abu Dhabi's MGX among investors, plus Nvidia and Cisco

July 2025 Grok posts praised Hitler and blamed people with Jewish surnames for 'anti-white' activism; xAI: 'has taken action to ban hate speech before Grok posts on X'; ADL: 'irresponsible, dangerous and antisemitic'

de11_money.topic: Musk political money 2024-2026, sweepstakes, Wisconsin, America Party, PSI report

claims.text: 2024: Musk spent more than $290M; about a quarter billion to America PAC, including $11.2M on 31 Dec 2024 for 'petition incentives'; giveaways cost more than $50M; $10,000 checks to dozens of state Republican parties

Musk 19 Oct 2024: money awarded 'randomly to people who have signed the petition'; 20 Oct: 'a daily chance of winning $1M!'; PAC lawyer Gober in court 4 Nov 2024: 'The $1 million recipients are not chosen by chance'; director Young testified winners vetted and signed NDAs; Judge Foglietta let it continue; Krasner had sued
Wisconsin Supreme Court, 1 April 2025: Crawford beat Musk-backed Schimel by 10 points; Musk spent more than $20M, about 1 in $5 in the race; paid petition signers and handed $1M checks in Green Bay

5 July 2025 Musk said he formed the America Party 'to give you back your freedom', after threatening to if 'this insane spending bill passes'; no confirmed FEC registration; Trump called it 'ridiculous'

AP 12 Oct 2026: since July 2026 more than $276M: SLF $158M, America PAC $76M, Lone Star Liberty PAC $10M (Paxton); confirmed by spokesman Romeo; in May 2025 Musk had said 'I think I've done enough'; reconciled with Trump, who presented him the National Medal of Science on 8 Oct 2026

America PAC pre-general FEC report (filed 22 Oct 2026): Musk $12.6M (6 Oct), $19M (8 Oct), $43.2M (14 Oct); $1.98M to United States of America Inc.; SLF $75M (9 Sep) and $83M (23 Sep), each passed next day to Texas PAC; about $366M by end of September; known cycle total past $440M

PSI minority staff memo (27 April 2025): at least $2.37bn potential liability for 40 of 65 actions involving Musk companies; 25 more unestimated; Tesla Autopilot/FSD $1.19bn; DOJ dismissed a SpaceX civil action (Feb 2025); potential, not assessed, liability

de11_claims.topic: Musk claims against the record: funding secured, robotaxi timelines, DOGE savings, Epstein, gesture, feud

claims.text: 7 Aug 2018 tweet: could take Tesla private at $420, funding secured; SEC alleged he had not discussed specific terms including price with financing partners and lacked adequate basis; settled 29 Sept 2018 without admitting or denying: $20M penalty each for Musk and Tesla, Musk steps down as chairman for three years
Judge Edward Chen had ruled the tweets false and reckless; jury found Musk not liable on 3 Feb 2023; Musk testified he believed he had a handshake deal with Saudi PIF, 'no ill motive'

Oct 2016 promised LA-to-New York autonomous demo by end 2017 (not met); Apr 2019 'next year for sure, we'll have over a million robotaxis on the road' (not met); Jul 2020 level 5 'complete this year' (not met); Jan 2025 unsupervised paid service in Austin in June; launched 22 June 2025 with a safety monitor
22 Jan 2026: first Tesla robotaxi rides without a safety monitor in Austin; 'a few' vehicles unsupervised; small fleet; 2025 predictions of unsupervised rides by year-end were well off the mark
27 Oct 2024 MSG rally: 'I think we can do at least $2 trillion'; FY2024 spending $6.75tn

10 April 2025 cabinet meeting: 'we anticipate savings in '26 from reduction of waste and fraud by $150 billion'; website claimed ~$150bn, published a sample; errors ($8bn contract actually $8M), more than 1,000 cancellations removed erasing ~$4bn

16 Musk-Epstein emails 2012-13 in DOJ release: 24 Nov 2012 'What day/night will be the wildest party on your island?'; Jan 2013 Musk cancelled ('Logistics won't work'); 26 Feb 2013 Epstein 'thanks for the tour' after SpaceX visit, calendar lunch; Dec 2013 Musk 'Is there a good time to visit?', Epstein cancelled 30 Dec; 4 Jul 2020 Musk 'To the best our knowledge, he never toured SpaceX'; 2026 Musk 'declined repeated invitations to go to his island'; no visit documented; no indication of wrongdoing

20 Jan 2025 gesture at Capital One Arena; ADL: 'an awkward gesture in a moment of enthusiasm, not a Nazi salute'; historians split (Ben-Ghiat: Nazi salute; Astor: not); Musk: critics need 'better dirty tricks', 'The everyone is Hitler attack is sooo tired'

5 June 2025: Trump said the easiest way to save billions was to 'terminate Elon's governmental subsidies and contracts'; Musk claimed Trump would have lost without him and alleged without evidence that Trump was in the Epstein files

13 Feb 2025 (World Governments Summit, by video): 'I think we do need to delete entire agencies'; 'If we don't remove the roots of the weed, then it's easy for the weed to grow back'; 'rule of the bureaucracy as opposed to rule of the people — democracy'
